title: decision-record template variables
description: Values for templates/decision-record.md.j2 and templates/decision-record.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from decision-record.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

chosen_model.title: Chosen model
chosen_model.description: Model and version you are committing to. The version matters - providers reissue a name and the vectors from the two are not comparable, let alone interchangeable.

compliance_flags.title: Compliance flags
compliance_flags.description: PII, air-gap or data-residency constraints that rule providers out. If there are none, write none - an unexamined "none" is how customer records end up in a hosted embedding API.

corpus_profile.title: Corpus profile
corpus_profile.description: Size, language mix and growth rate of what you will embed. Name the languages - multilingual content against an English-tuned model is the exact failure this record exists to prevent.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.description: Vector dimensions you will store. It sets index size and memory cost directly, and reducing it later means re-embedding the whole corpus behind a dual-write window.

latency_sla.title: Latency sla
latency_sla.description: The p50 and p95 query latency you must stay inside, and the cost per thousand queries you can afford. Both, with numbers - a choice made on quality alone gets reversed by the invoice.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Who serves it - openai, cohere, self-hosted. Self-hosting moves the cost from invoice to ops time; say which side you have chosen to pay on, because both are real.
